reason: The text contains named characters who are not leaders. Most notably, Chamutal (חֲמוּטַל), identified as the mother of King Zedekiah ('וְשֵׁם אִמּוֹ חֲמוּטַל בַּֽת־ יִרְמְיָהוּ'), is explicitly named but has no leadership role—she is only identified by her relationship to the king. Similarly, Achikam (אֲחִיקָם) and Shafan (שָׁפָן) appear as named ancestors in genealogy ('בֶּן־ אֲחִיקָם בֶּן־ שָׁפָן') without any leadership position ascribed to them in this passage. While most other named figures (Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, Gedaliah, and the priests Seraiah and Zephaniah) are clearly leaders, the existence of named non-leaders contradicts the claim that 'only' leaders are named.
